request.spec:
A steward can waive a claim's late charge (a button on an OPEN or PENDING claim; CLAIM_WAIVED
naming the claim; anyone else, any other status, or a claim already waived is refused with an error
on the claim). A waived claim bears no late charge from then on, whatever its overdue state; show
waived yes/no on the claim.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can waive a claim's late charge (a button on an OPEN or PENDING claim; CLAIM_WAIVED
naming the claim; anyone else, any other status, or a claim already waived is refused with an error
on the claim). A waived claim bears no late charge from then on, whatever its overdue state; show

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The waiver is implemented and the spec passes except one line, and that line is a defect in the spec itself. Against the unmodified spec, 3 of 4 tests pass. The 4th, "late charge waiver scenario 2", fails only at `acceptance.spec.ts:713`. That line expects the sheet parent to read the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`, which looks like a placeholder that was never filled in. Line 620 sets the parent to `${sheet}-p` and the audit check at line 917 expects the real sheet id, and the app shows the real value (e.g. `smvks10sbki6k-p`). No correct app can pass that assertion. I ran a temporary copy with only that line corrected and scenario 2 passed in full, then deleted the copy. I didn't edit the real spec, as instructed.

**What I changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V99__claim_waived.sql`, adds a `waived` flag to claims and claim history. Cloning a sheet copies the flag.
- **Server:** a new endpoint `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/waive`, modelled on the existing "remind" action. It refuses with an error unless the user is a steward, the claim is OPEN or PENDING, and it isn't already waived. A refusal writes nothing. A success writes `CLAIM_WAIVED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=… number=…`.
- **Late charge:** a waived claim is charged nothing, both on the server and in the front end's own copy of the calculation. It can still show as overdue.
- **Front end:** each claim row shows `claim-waived` (yes/no) and has a `claim-waive` button; a refusal appears in `claim-error`.
- **Split claims:** when a claim is split, the new part starts unwaived and the original keeps its flag. The request didn't cover this, so change it if you'd rather the new part stay waived too.

**Two things about running `bin/e2e` on this machine**
- **Startup is too slow for it.** The machine is heavily loaded (load around 18 on 8 cores) and the app took 40–60 seconds or more to start. `bin/e2e` waits only 60 seconds, so my first run tested before the app was up and everything failed. I worked around it by starting the app myself, waiting until it was healthy, then running the same Playwright tests.
- **Use a separate port.** Other copies of this app are running on ports 3002–3004. One of my runs on port 3000 overlapped with my own previous instance, which was still shutting down, and gave a false failure (a person's name showed as `Fay (C)`). On port 3010 that problem went away; the results above are from that port.
